regiones/tierra-santa/resumen.texto: The land between the Mediterranean and the Jordan, sacred to Jews, Christians and Muslims: Canaan, the Land of Israel, Judea, Palestine, the Latin Kingdom of Jerusalem and, today, Israel and the Palestinian territories. It changed hands more than almost any other region in the world, and each faith read it through its own texts.

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.15.nombre.texto: Ayyubids and the Kingdom of Acre

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.0.resumen.texto: Hunter-gatherers who settled in permanent villages before agriculture, on Mount Carmel and in the Jordan Valley.

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.1.resumen.texto: Agriculture, the first large villages and the Tower of Jericho, one of the oldest structures in the world.

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.2.resumen.texto: Villages of farmers and herders who smelt copper and bury their dead in dolmens. The Ghassulian culture, known above all from Teleilat el-Ghassul near the Dead Sea, runs from 4400 to 3500 BC, and the era continues until 3300 BC.

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.3.resumen.texto: Canaanite city-states such as Hazor, Megiddo and Jerusalem, for centuries under Egyptian rule; the Amarna letters show their petty kings asking the pharaoh for help.

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.4.resumen.texto: After the collapse of the Bronze Age, the Israelites emerge in the hills and the Philistines on the coast. Israel, with its capital at Samaria, falls to Assyria in 722 BC; Judah, with Jerusalem and its temple, falls to Babylon in 586 BC.

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.5.resumen.texto: Exile in Babylon and return under Cyrus; the Persian province of Yehud rebuilds the temple and, with Ezra and Nehemiah, establishes the Torah as law.

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.6.resumen.texto: After Alexander, the region passes from Egypt to the Seleucids; the forced Hellenization by Antiochus IV provokes the Maccabean revolt.

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.7.resumen.texto: Independent Jewish state of the Maccabees, which expands through Idumea, Samaria and Galilee; from 63 BC it falls under Roman protection.

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.8.resumen.texto: Herod rebuilds the temple; during this period Jesus of Nazareth and his first followers live. The wars against Rome end with the destruction of the temple in 70 and the defeat of Bar Kokhba in 135.

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.9.resumen.texto: Jerusalem is refounded as Aelia Capitolina, closed to Jews; the center of Jewish life moves to Galilee, where the Mishnah is compiled.

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.10.resumen.texto: Constantine and his mother Helena fill the region with churches; pilgrims and monks make it the Christian Holy Land. The Persians occupy it between 614 and 628.

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.11.resumen.texto: The Arabs conquer the region after Yarmouk; the caliph Abd al-Malik builds the Dome of the Rock and Ramla is founded as the capital of the province of Filastin.

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.12.resumen.texto: The region is on the periphery of Baghdad and then falls under dynasties from Egypt; the population is slowly Islamized and Arabized.

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.13.resumen.texto: The Shiite caliphs of Cairo and the Seljuk Turks compete for Syria and Palestine; the caliph al-Hakim destroys the Holy Sepulchre in 1009.

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.14.resumen.texto: Crusader state founded after the capture of Jerusalem in 1099, with military orders, castles and Italian port cities.

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.15.resumen.texto: Saladin retakes Jerusalem; the Crusaders keep the coast from Acre until the Mamluks take it in 1291. Jerusalem returns to Christian hands through a treaty between 1229 and 1244.

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.16.resumen.texto: The Mamluks of Cairo level the coastal ports to prevent new crusades; Jerusalem is a city of madrasas and pilgrimage.

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.17.resumen.texto: Suleiman rebuilds the walls of Jerusalem; Safed is a major center of Kabbalah in the 16th century. In the 19th century European consuls, missions, biblical archaeology and the first Zionist colonies arrive.

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.18.resumen.texto: Great Britain conquers the region in 1917 and governs it under a League of Nations mandate that includes the Balfour Declaration. Zionism and Palestinian Arab nationalism grow at the same time, in open clash from 1920.

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.19.resumen.texto: After the 1948 war, the State of Israel occupies most of the territory; Jordan annexes the West Bank and East Jerusalem, and Egypt administers Gaza. Hundreds of thousands of Palestinians become refugees.

regiones/tierra-santa/eras.20.resumen.texto: Israel occupies the West Bank, East Jerusalem, Gaza and the Golan in the Six-Day War. Since the Oslo Accords (1993) the Palestinian Authority administers part of the West Bank; Hamas has governed Gaza since 2007.

regiones/tierra-santa/demografia.0.nota.texto: 1st century. A high and disputed estimate: other authors, such as Broshi (1979), put it at about one million inhabitants, and Wikipedia summarizes 1 to 1.5 million for the Byzantine-era peak.

regiones/tierra-santa/demografia.2.nota.texto: Ottoman tax registers of 1533–1539: about 145,000 Muslims, 6,000 Christians and 5,000 Jews.

regiones/tierra-santa/demografia.10.nota.texto: 1,061,270 Muslims, 553,600 Jews and 135,550 Christians (official estimate, not a census).

regiones/tierra-santa/demografia.12.nota.texto: Israel (9.8 million, including East Jerusalem and the Golan) plus the West Bank and Gaza (5.5 million). The two statistics offices count the inhabitants of East Jerusalem differently.

regiones/tierra-santa/religiones.0.nota.texto: Baal, El, Asherah and Astarte; the Yahwism of the Israelites arises from this religious world and gradually separates from it.

regiones/tierra-santa/religiones.2.nota.texto: It was the majority religion in Judea and Galilee; Greco-Roman cults dominated in the coastal cities and the Decapolis.

regiones/tierra-santa/religiones.4.nota.texto: They were numerous until the 6th-century revolts against Justinian; fewer than a thousand remain today, on Mount Gerizim and in Holon.

regiones/tierra-santa/religiones.7.nota.texto: By the 5th century Christians were the majority; after the Arab conquest, conversion to Islam was slow and its pace is debated.

regiones/tierra-santa/religiones.10.nota.texto: The Muslim majority took shape between the 9th and 13th centuries; Ellenblum (1998) shows that many Christian villages still existed at the time of the crusades.

regiones/tierra-santa/religiones.13.nota.texto: In Galilee and on Mount Carmel.

regiones/tierra-santa/religiones.14.nota.texto: Its world center is in Haifa and Acre, where its founder, Bahá'u'lláh, died in exile in 1892.

regiones/tierra-santa/religiones.15.nota.texto: The majority religion in Israel and the territories as a whole since 1948; in the West Bank and Gaza the great majority is Muslim.

regiones/tierra-santa/culturas.8.nombre.texto: Turkish (Mamluks and Ottomans, as an elite)

regiones/tierra-santa/culturas.2.nota.texto: The Philistines arrived by sea in the 12th century BC and founded five cities on the southern coast; they disappear as a people after the Babylonian conquest of 604 BC.

regiones/tierra-santa/culturas.6.nota.texto: Since 1948 Arab culture has been the majority in the West Bank and Gaza and a minority within Israel.

regiones/tierra-santa/culturas.10.nota.texto: Mainly Ashkenazim, Sephardim and Jews from the Arab countries and Iran (Mizrahim), and since 1990 nearly a million immigrants from the former Soviet Union.

regiones/tierra-santa/idiomas.1.nota.texto: The language of Jesus, of the spoken Mishnah and of the Jerusalem Talmud.

regiones/tierra-santa/idiomas.2.nota.texto: Language of the temple and of the Dead Sea Scrolls; from the 3rd century it survives as a language of liturgy and books.

regiones/tierra-santa/idiomas.4.nota.texto: Since 1948 it has been so in the West Bank and Gaza; in Israel it is the language of a fifth of the population.

regiones/tierra-santa/idiomas.9.nota.texto: Revived as a spoken language in the late 19th century by Eliezer Ben-Yehuda and the schools of the settlements.

regiones/libano/resumen.texto: The coast of the Phoenician cities (Byblos, Sidon, Tyre) and Mount Lebanon, a refuge for Maronites and Druze. It was the crusader County of Tripoli, a Mamluk and Ottoman province, and since 1943 a country shared among religious communities.

regiones/libano/eras.0.resumen.texto: Seafaring city-states that spread the alphabet and founded Carthage.

regiones/libano/eras.1.resumen.texto: Beirut has a famous school of Roman law until the earthquake of 551; Baalbek, its great temples.

regiones/libano/eras.2.resumen.texto: Arab conquest; the Maronites withdraw into the mountains. The Druze emerge in the 11th century.

regiones/libano/eras.3.resumen.texto: Crusader state; the Maronites enter into union with Rome. The Mamluks take Tripoli in 1289.

regiones/libano/eras.5.resumen.texto: Druze and Maronite emirates in the mountains; civil war of 1860 and autonomy of Mount Lebanon.

regiones/libano/eras.6.resumen.texto: After the Ottoman defeat, the coast is administered by France as part of the Occupied Enemy Territory (OETA West) until the San Remo conference (April 1920) grants it the mandate. The Bekaa depends on Faisal (OETA East) until Maysalun (July 1920).

regiones/libano/eras.8.resumen.texto: Power-sharing among confessional communities; civil war (1975–1990), Syrian and Israeli occupations, and the rise of Hezbollah.

regiones/libano/religiones.2.nota.texto: In union with Rome since the time of the crusades.

regiones/siria/resumen.texto: The interior of the Levant, from Damascus to Aleppo and Antioch. Heart of the Umayyad Caliphate, front line of the wars between Byzantines and Arabs, land of the northern crusader principalities and of the great leaders of the jihad against them, Zengi, Nur al-Din and Saladin.

regiones/siria/eras.1.nombre.texto: Aramean kingdoms and Assyrian and Persian rule

regiones/siria/eras.6.nombre.texto: Crusader Antioch and Zengid and Ayyubid Syria

regiones/siria/eras.9.nombre.texto: Faisal's administration and the Arab Kingdom of Syria

regiones/siria/eras.0.resumen.texto: Bronze Age kingdoms with great archives of tablets.

regiones/siria/eras.1.resumen.texto: Damascus is the capital of Aram; the Assyrians take it in 732 BC.

regiones/siria/eras.2.resumen.texto: Antioch, founded in 300 BC, is the capital.

regiones/siria/eras.3.resumen.texto: Antioch is one of the great cities of the Empire and the seat of a patriarchate; Palmyra rebels under Zenobia.

regiones/siria/eras.4.resumen.texto: Damascus is the capital of an empire stretching from the Indus to the Pyrenees.

regiones/siria/eras.5.resumen.texto: Aleppo is the court of Sayf al-Dawla and Al-Farabi; the Byzantines retake Antioch in 969.

regiones/siria/eras.6.resumen.texto: The Principality of Antioch in the north; Zengi, Nur al-Din and Saladin unite Aleppo and Damascus.

regiones/siria/eras.7.resumen.texto: After repelling the Mongols, the Mamluks rule from Cairo; Tamerlane sacks Damascus in 1401.

regiones/siria/eras.8.resumen.texto: Damascus is the gateway for the pilgrim caravan to Mecca.

regiones/siria/eras.9.resumen.texto: Faisal governs the interior from 1918 and, after the British withdrawal of 1919, proclaims the kingdom on March 8, 1920; France defeats it at Maysalun in July.

regiones/siria/eras.10.resumen.texto: France defeats Faisal's Arab kingdom at Maysalun.

regiones/siria/eras.11.resumen.texto: Coups d'état, the Baath party and the Assad dynasty from 1970; civil war since 2011 and the fall of Bashar al-Assad in 2024.

regiones/siria/demografia.0.nota.texto: Syria within its current borders (including the Jazira, which the Mesopotamia polygon also covers).

regiones/siria/religiones.5.nota.texto: In the coastal mountains; the Assad family belongs to this community.

regiones/siria/religiones.7.nota.texto: They held castles in the Syrian mountains, such as Masyaf.

regiones/transjordania/resumen.texto: The lands east of the Jordan and the Dead Sea: Ammon, Moab and Edom in the Bible, the Nabataean kingdom of Petra, the cities of the Decapolis, the crusader lordship of Oultrejordain and, since 1921, the Hashemite kingdom of Jordan.

regiones/transjordania/eras.0.resumen.texto: Iron Age kingdoms; the Mesha Stele recounts Moab's rebellion against Israel.

regiones/transjordania/eras.1.resumen.texto: Incense traders with their capital at Petra.

regiones/transjordania/eras.2.resumen.texto: Trajan annexes the Nabataean kingdom; Jerash, Gadara and Philadelphia (Amman) are Greek cities of the Decapolis.

regiones/transjordania/eras.3.resumen.texto: The Battle of Yarmouk, on the northern border, decides the Arab conquest of the Levant.

regiones/transjordania/eras.4.resumen.texto: The castles of Kerak and Montreal on the route to Mecca; Raynald of Châtillon raids the caravans from there.

regiones/transjordania/eras.6.resumen.texto: A tribal region crossed by the pilgrim caravan.

regiones/transjordania/eras.7.resumen.texto: The region depends on the Hashemite government of Faisal and, from 1920, on his Syrian kingdom, until Maysalun.

regiones/transjordania/eras.8.resumen.texto: After Maysalun it was left without a central government. Abdullah entered in November 1920 and settled in Amman in March 1921.

regiones/transjordania/eras.9.resumen.texto: Abdullah, son of the Sharif of Mecca, governs under British mandate.

regiones/transjordania/eras.10.resumen.texto: Annexes the West Bank between 1950 and 1967; signs peace with Israel in 1994.

regiones/arabia/resumen.texto: The Arabian Peninsula: the incense kingdoms of the south, the oases and caravan cities of the Hejaz and, in Mecca and Medina, the cradle of Islam. From there, in the 7th century, began the expansion that within a hundred years reached from the Indus to the Pyrenees.

regiones/arabia/eras.3.nombre.texto: Mecca and Medina under caliphs and sultans

regiones/arabia/eras.5.nombre.texto: Kingdom of Hejaz and the Saudi conquest

regiones/arabia/eras.6.nombre.texto: Saudi Arabia and the Gulf States

regiones/arabia/eras.0.resumen.texto: Saba, Ma'in and Himyar in Yemen; the Nabataeans and the cities of the Hejaz on the incense route. In the 6th century the Himyarite king Dhu Nuwas, a convert to Judaism, persecutes the Christians of Najran.

regiones/arabia/eras.1.resumen.texto: Ethiopians and Persians fight over Yemen; Mecca, with its sanctuary of the Kaaba, is a commercial center of the Quraysh tribe.

regiones/arabia/eras.2.resumen.texto: Muhammad preaches in Mecca, emigrates to Medina in 622 and unifies Arabia; his successors conquer Persia, Syria and Egypt.

regiones/arabia/eras.3.resumen.texto: The capital moves to Damascus, Baghdad and Cairo; the holy cities come under the Sharifs of Mecca.

regiones/arabia/eras.4.resumen.texto: The Ottoman sultan is “Servant of the Two Holy Cities.” In Najd, Wahhabism arises in the 18th century, allied with the House of Saud.

regiones/arabia/eras.5.resumen.texto: Sharif Hussein rebels against the Ottomans with British support; Ibn Saud defeats him in 1925.

regiones/arabia/eras.6.resumen.texto: Oil transforms the peninsula; Yemen, Oman and the emirates are separate states.

regiones/arabia/demografia.0.nota.texto: Sum of the countries of the Arabian Peninsula.

regiones/arabia/religiones.4.nombre.texto: Shiite Islam (Zaydis in Yemen, Shiites in the east)

regiones/arabia/religiones.1.nota.texto: In Yemen and in Hejaz oases such as Yathrib (Medina) and Khaybar.

regiones/arabia/religiones.2.nota.texto: In Najran, Yemen and among northern tribes.

regiones/magreb/resumen.texto: North Africa west of Egypt, from Cyrenaica to the Atlantic: Phoenician Carthage, Augustine's Roman Africa, the Vandal kingdom and the Byzantine province conquered by the Arabs between 647 and 709, from which the conquest of Hispania was launched in 711.

regiones/magreb/eras.4.nombre.texto: Arab conquest and the Umayyad Maghreb

regiones/magreb/eras.0.resumen.texto: Phoenician colony that dominated the western Mediterranean until its destruction by Rome.

regiones/magreb/eras.1.resumen.texto: Provinces rich in grain and olive oil and one of the centers of Latin Christianity, with Tertullian, Cyprian and Augustine.

regiones/magreb/eras.2.resumen.texto: The Arian Vandals take Carthage in 439 and persecute the Catholics.

regiones/magreb/eras.3.resumen.texto: Justinian reconquers the region; it resists the Arabs until the fall of Carthage in 698.

regiones/magreb/eras.4.resumen.texto: Uqba ibn Nafi founds Kairouan in 670; the Berbers resist under Kusaila and the Kahina and later make up the bulk of the armies that cross into Hispania.

regiones/magreb/eras.5.resumen.texto: Regional dynasties; Fez is founded in 789 and its al-Qarawiyyin mosque in 859. The Fatimids set out from here to conquer Egypt.

regiones/magreb/eras.6.resumen.texto: Berber empires that unite the Maghreb and al-Andalus from Marrakesh.

regiones/magreb/eras.7.resumen.texto: Kingdoms of Tunis, Tlemcen and Fez; Ibn Khaldun writes his Muqaddimah here.

regiones/magreb/eras.8.resumen.texto: Algiers, Tunis and Tripoli under the Ottomans and their corsairs; Morocco independent under the Saadians and Alaouites.

regiones/magreb/eras.9.resumen.texto: France conquers Algeria from 1830 and establishes protectorates over Tunisia and Morocco; Italy takes Libya.

regiones/magreb/eras.10.resumen.texto: Libya, Tunisia, Morocco and, after an eight-year war, Algeria.

regiones/magreb/demografia.0.nota.texto: Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya and Western Sahara in their entirety, including their Saharan parts.

regiones/magreb/religiones.1.nota.texto: With the Donatist schism in the 4th and 5th centuries.

regiones/magreb/religiones.4.nota.texto: The Ibadi Kharijites founded the Rustamid imamate of Tahert; they survive today in the Mzab and on Djerba.

regiones/magreb/religiones.6.nota.texto: Very ancient communities, reinforced by the Sephardim expelled from Spain in 1492; nearly all emigrated between 1948 and 1970.

regiones/magreb/culturas.1.nota.texto: Indigenous peoples of the Maghreb, predating Carthage (814 BC), with which this region's record begins.

regiones/magreb/idiomas.0.nota.texto: Indigenous peoples of the Maghreb, predating Carthage (814 BC), with which this region's record begins.

regiones/chipre/resumen.texto: The large island of the eastern Mediterranean: Byzantine and contested with the Arabs, conquered by Richard the Lionheart in 1191 and then the kingdom of the Lusignans, a refuge for the crusaders after the fall of Acre, Venetian and Ottoman; divided since 1974.

regiones/chipre/eras.0.resumen.texto: City-kingdoms such as Salamis, Paphos and Kition, under the Assyrians, Egyptians and Persians.

regiones/chipre/eras.1.resumen.texto: Paul and Barnabas preach on the island, which has had an autocephalous Church since 431.

regiones/chipre/eras.2.resumen.texto: After Muawiya's raids in 649, the island remains neutral and pays tribute to both empires.

regiones/chipre/eras.4.resumen.texto: Guy of Lusignan, the deposed king of Jerusalem, buys the island; after 1291 it is the base of the crusaders and Latin merchants.

regiones/chipre/eras.5.resumen.texto: Venice fortifies Nicosia and Famagusta, which fall to the Ottomans in 1570–1571.

regiones/chipre/eras.8.resumen.texto: Independent in 1960; the Turkish invasion of 1974 divides the island.

regiones/chipre/religiones.0.nombre.texto: Greek and Phoenician religion (Aphrodite of Paphos)

regiones/armenia/resumen.texto: The plateau between the Euphrates, Lake Van, Lake Sevan and the Kura, around Mount Ararat. It was the heartland of the kingdom of Urartu and later of the Armenian kingdoms; according to tradition, Armenia adopted Christianity as its state religion c. 301, and Mesrop Mashtots created its alphabet c. 405. After centuries of Persian, Byzantine, Arab, Seljuk, Ottoman and Russian rule, the genocide of 1915 eliminated the Armenians from the western part, now Turkish; the eastern part is the Republic of Armenia. Religions, cultures and languages are recorded up to 1920; after that, the Turkish part is covered by the Anatolia region.

regiones/armenia/eras.9.nombre.texto: Soviet Armenia and Republic of Armenia

regiones/armenia/eras.0.resumen.texto: Kingdom of Biainili, with its capital at Tushpa, by Lake Van, a rival of Assyria.

regiones/armenia/eras.1.resumen.texto: Armenia is a Persian satrapy governed by the Orontids; the Behistun inscription already names it c. 520 BC.

regiones/armenia/eras.2.resumen.texto: The Orontids rule autonomously under Alexander and the Seleucids.

regiones/armenia/eras.3.resumen.texto: Tigranes the Great (95–55 BC) builds a short-lived empire; Armenia then lies between Rome and Parthia, and the Arsacid king Tiridates III adopts Christianity.

regiones/armenia/eras.4.resumen.texto: After the Arsacids, Armenia is divided between Persia and Byzantium; at Avarayr (451) the Armenians defend Christianity, and from the 7th century it is ruled by the caliphate.

regiones/armenia/eras.5.resumen.texto: Ashot I is recognized as king in 885; Ani becomes one of the great cities of the Caucasus.

regiones/armenia/eras.6.resumen.texto: Byzantium annexes Ani in 1045 and the Seljuks take it in 1064; many Armenians emigrate to Cilicia; later Georgia, the Mongols and the Turkoman confederations dominate.

regiones/armenia/eras.7.resumen.texto: After the Battle of Chaldiran (1514) and the Peace of Amasya (1555), the west is Ottoman and the east, Persian.

regiones/armenia/eras.8.resumen.texto: Russia takes Yerevan in 1828; in the Ottoman Empire, the Hamidian massacres (1894–1896) and the genocide of 1915 destroy the Armenian population; in 1918 the First Republic of Armenia is born.

regiones/armenia/eras.9.resumen.texto: Eastern Armenia is a Soviet republic from 1920 and independent from 1991; the western part is part of Turkey.

regiones/armenia/demografia.0.nota.texto: Republic of Armenia only; historical Western Armenia is counted with Turkey (Anatolia region).

regiones/armenia/religiones.1.nombre.texto: Pre-Christian Armenian religion, of Iranian origin (Aramazd, Anahit, Mihr)

regiones/cilicia/resumen.texto: The coastal plain of southeastern Anatolia, between the Taurus Mountains and the Gulf of Alexandretta, with Tarsus, Adana and Sis. An obligatory passage between Anatolia and Syria through the Cilician Gates, from 1080 to 1375 it was the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia, an ally of the crusaders and of the Mongols against the Mamluks.

regiones/cilicia/eras.3.nombre.texto: Byzantine Cilicia and frontier with Islam

regiones/cilicia/eras.0.resumen.texto: Hurrian and Luwian kingdom that passes into the Hittite orbit.

regiones/cilicia/eras.1.resumen.texto: The Luwian kingdom of Que (Hiyawa) falls to Assyria in the 8th century BC; under the Persians it is ruled by kings called Syennesis.

regiones/cilicia/eras.2.resumen.texto: Alexander wins at Issus (333 BC); Rome makes it a province, and Tarsus, birthplace of the apostle Paul, is its capital.

regiones/cilicia/eras.3.resumen.texto: Frontier between Byzantium and the caliphate from the 7th century; Nikephoros Phokas recovers it in 965.

regiones/cilicia/eras.4.resumen.texto: Principality of the Rubenids from 1080 and kingdom from 1198, with its capital at Sis; an ally of the crusaders and of the Mongols, it falls to the Mamluks in 1375.

regiones/cilicia/eras.5.resumen.texto: The Ramadanids, a Turkoman beylik, rule Adana under the Mamluks.

regiones/cilicia/eras.6.resumen.texto: Part of the Ottoman Empire; in 1909 the Adana massacres kill thousands of Armenians.

regiones/cilicia/eras.7.resumen.texto: Turkish provinces of Mersin, Adana and Osmaniye.

fuentes/tora/autor.texto: Israelite tradition, written by several hands

fuentes/tora/resumen.texto: The five books of Moses: Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy. They narrate the creation, the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the slavery in Egypt, the exodus and the law given at Sinai, and end with the people at the gates of the promised land of Canaan.

fuentes/tora/por_que_importa.texto: It is the core of Judaism and the first part of the Christian Bible; the Quran recognizes it as a revelation given to Moses (Tawrat). The promise of the land to Abraham's descendants lies at the center of the entire later history of the region. Scholars debate when and how its sources were brought together; much research places its final form in the Persian period.

fuentes/tanaj/resumen.texto: The twenty-four books of the Jewish Bible: the Torah, the Prophets (the history of Israel and Judah from Joshua to the exile, plus Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel and the twelve minor prophets) and the Writings (Psalms, Proverbs, Job, Daniel, Ezra, Nehemiah, Chronicles and others). For Christians it is the Old Testament.

fuentes/tanaj/por_que_importa.texto: It is the main written source on ancient Israel and the founding text of Judaism and Christianity; its historical value is debated book by book in the light of archaeology and inscriptions.

fuentes/septuaginta/resumen.texto: Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible made in Alexandria from the 3rd century BC; according to the Letter of Aristeas, by seventy-two scholars sent from Jerusalem for the library of Ptolemy II.

fuentes/septuaginta/por_que_importa.texto: It was the Bible of Greek-speaking Jews and of the first Christians, who quote it in the New Testament; the Orthodox Churches still use it.

fuentes/nuevo-testamento/resumen.texto: Twenty-seven Christian writings: the four gospels on the life, death and resurrection of Jesus, the Acts of the Apostles, the letters of Paul and of other apostles, and the Book of Revelation.

fuentes/nuevo-testamento/por_que_importa.texto: It is the founding text of Christianity and the main source on Jesus and on the first community in Jerusalem. Some of its passages about “the Jews” were used for centuries to justify Christian anti-Judaism, which the Catholic Church repudiated in 1965.

fuentes/vulgata/resumen.texto: Latin translation of the Bible that Jerome made in Bethlehem, largely directly from the Hebrew, with the help of Jewish teachers, instead of translating the Septuagint.

fuentes/vulgata/por_que_importa.texto: It was the Bible of the Latin Church for more than a thousand years and the first book printed by Gutenberg; the Council of Trent declared it authentic.

fuentes/manuscritos-del-mar-muerto/resum.texto: Some 900 manuscripts found between 1947 and 1956 in eleven caves near Qumran: copies of every book of the Hebrew Bible except Esther, a thousand years older than those known until then, apocryphal texts, and the writings of a sect that saw itself as the “sons of light” in opposition to the temple of Jerusalem.

fuentes/manuscritos-del-mar-muerto/por_q.texto: They transformed the study of the biblical text and of Judaism in the time of Jesus. Most are kept in the Shrine of the Book in Jerusalem and have been digitized.

fuentes/manuscritos-del-mar-muerto/leer..texto: Leon Levy Dead Sea Scrolls Digital Library (Israel Antiquities Authority)

fuentes/gran-rollo-de-isaias/resumen.texto: Complete copy of the Book of Isaiah found in Qumran Cave 1 in 1947.

fuentes/gran-rollo-de-isaias/por_que_imp.texto: It is the oldest known complete biblical manuscript and agrees in essentials with the medieval Masoretic text, which showed the faithfulness of Jewish transmission.

fuentes/regla-de-la-comunidad/resumen.texto: Rules on admission, communal life, purity and punishments of a community set apart from the temple of Jerusalem, with the doctrine of the two spirits, of truth and of perversity, that struggle within each person.

fuentes/regla-de-la-comunidad/por_que_im.texto: It is the key text for understanding the Qumran sect, which many scholars identify with the Essenes described by Josephus and Philo.

fuentes/rollo-de-la-guerra/resumen.texto: Manual for a forty-year war at the end of days between the “sons of light” and the “sons of darkness” and their allies the Kittim, probably the Romans, with banners, trumpets, formations and prayers.

fuentes/rollo-de-la-guerra/por_que_impor.texto: It shows how part of Judaism conceived of eschatological holy war shortly before the revolt against Rome.

fuentes/rollo-del-templo/resumen.texto: The longest scroll from Qumran: a law dictated by God in the first person, with the plan of an ideal temple and rules on purity, the king and war.

fuentes/rollo-de-cobre/resumen.texto: List engraved in metal of 64 hiding places of gold, silver and cult objects, perhaps from the temple, in Jerusalem and the Judean Desert. None has ever been found.

fuentes/primer-libro-de-los-macabeos/res.texto: History of the revolt against the Seleucids from Antiochus IV to John Hyrcanus: Mattathias, the victories of Judas Maccabeus, the purification of the Temple and the independence of Judea. In its praise of Rome (8:2) it counts among Rome's exploits the wars against the Galatians, whom it says Rome subjected to tribute.

fuentes/primer-libro-de-los-macabeos/por.texto: It is the main source on the Maccabean revolt. It is part of the Catholic and Orthodox Bibles, not of the Jewish or Protestant ones.

fuentes/misna/resumen.texto: First written compilation of the Jewish oral law, in six orders: agriculture, festivals, women, damages, holy things and purities. It records the dissenting opinions of the sages of two centuries.

fuentes/misna/por_que_importa.texto: It is the basis of the Talmud and of all Jewish law; it shows how Judaism reorganized itself after the loss of the temple.

fuentes/talmud-de-jerusalen/resumen.texto: Commentary on the Mishnah compiled in the academies of Tiberias, Sepphoris and Caesarea, shorter and less polished than the Babylonian one.

fuentes/talmud-de-babilonia/resumen.texto: Vast commentary on the Mishnah developed over three centuries in the Jewish academies of Sasanian Mesopotamia, with legal discussions, stories, medicine and ethics.

fuentes/talmud-de-babilonia/por_que_impo.texto: It is the central text of Jewish study to this day.

fuentes/coran/autor.texto: Revealed to Muhammad, according to Islamic belief

fuentes/coran/soporte.texto: Oral recitation, written down on leaves and parchments; text fixed under Uthman c. 650

fuentes/coran/resumen.texto: Holy book of Islam, in 114 suras: the oneness of God, the Last Judgment, the stories of the prophets from Adam and Abraham to Moses and Jesus, and the rules of the community of Medina. For Muslims it is the literal word of God, communicated to Muhammad by the angel Gabriel.

fuentes/coran/por_que_importa.texto: It is the basis of the faith, of Islamic law and of Classical Arabic. It contains verses on war against unbelievers (such as 2:190–193, 9:5 and 9:29, which commands fighting “the People of the Book” until they pay tribute) and others of tolerance (“there is no compulsion in religion”, 2:256), which each era and each school interpreted in its own way.

fuentes/coran/leer.2.titulo.texto: English translation by J. M. Rodwell (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/coran/leer.3.titulo.texto: English translation by George Sale, 1734 (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/coran/leer.5.titulo.texto: French translation by Savary, 1783, on Wikisource

fuentes/manuscrito-de-birmingham/resumen.texto: Two leaves with parts of suras 18 to 20, whose parchment was radiocarbon-dated to between 568 and 645.

fuentes/manuscrito-de-birmingham/por_que.texto: They are among the oldest material witnesses of the Quran and match the current text.

fuentes/manuscrito-de-sana/resumen.texto: Palimpsest found in 1972 in the Great Mosque of Sanaa: the lower text, erased and written over, is a Quran with variants from the Uthmanic text.

fuentes/manuscrito-de-sana/por_que_impor.texto: It is the most important evidence that different versions circulated before standardization.

fuentes/sahih-al-bujari/resumen.texto: Collection of some 7,000 hadiths, sayings and deeds of Muhammad transmitted through chains of witnesses, arranged by topic: faith, prayer, trade, inheritance, jihad and the end of times.

fuentes/sahih-al-bujari/por_que_importa.texto: For Sunnis it is the most authoritative book after the Quran. Its book of jihad and apocalyptic hadiths such as that of the stones that betray hidden Jews (also in Sahih Muslim, with the gharqad tree) are quoted to this day, among others in the Hamas charter.

fuentes/sira-de-ibn-ishaq/titulo.texto: Life of the Messenger of God

fuentes/sira-de-ibn-ishaq/resumen.texto: First major biography of Muhammad, from his ancestors and the prophecies that foretold him to his death, with the Medina campaigns. It survives in the abridged version by Ibn Hisham (c. 830).

fuentes/sira-de-ibn-ishaq/por_que_import.texto: It is the source of almost everything told about Muhammad's life, although it was written more than a century after the events.

fuentes/sira-de-ibn-ishaq/leer.0.titulo.texto: Selection in English (Internet Islamic History Sourcebook, Fordham)

fuentes/constitucion-de-medina/resumen.texto: Pact between the emigrants from Mecca, the Arab tribes of Medina and their Jewish allies, who form a single community for common defense, “the Jews with their religion and the Muslims with theirs”.

fuentes/constitucion-de-medina/por_que_i.texto: It is the oldest political document of Islam; it is preserved in Ibn Ishaq, and how much of the original text it retains is debated.

fuentes/estela-de-merneptah/resumen.texto: Hymn to the victories of Pharaoh Merneptah that lists defeated peoples of Canaan: “Israel is laid waste, his seed is not”.

fuentes/estela-de-merneptah/por_que_impo.texto: It is the oldest mention of Israel outside the Bible.

fuentes/estela-de-tel-dan/resumen.texto: Fragments of a victory stele of an Aramean king, probably Hazael, who claims to have killed the king of Israel and the king of the “house of David”.

fuentes/estela-de-tel-dan/por_que_import.texto: It is the first mention of David outside the Bible.

fuentes/inscripcion-de-siloe/resumen.texto: Inscription in the tunnel that carries water from the Gihon Spring to the Pool of Siloam: it tells how the two teams of diggers, working from either end, met.

fuentes/inscripcion-de-siloe/por_que_imp.texto: It is one of the few monumental inscriptions in ancient Hebrew and confirms the work the Bible attributes to Hezekiah.

fuentes/prisma-de-senaquerib/resumen.texto: Account of the Assyrian king's campaigns, including that of 701 BC against Judah: he took 46 cities and shut Hezekiah up in Jerusalem “like a bird in a cage”.

fuentes/prisma-de-senaquerib/por_que_imp.texto: It allows one of the best-documented episodes in the history of Judah to be compared with the Bible.

fuentes/cartas-de-laquis/resumen.texto: Letters from an officer to his commander at Lachish during the Babylonian advance: “we are watching for the fire signals of Lachish, for we cannot see those of Azekah”.

fuentes/antiguedades-judias/resumen.texto: History of the Jewish people in twenty books, from the creation to the eve of the revolt of 66, written for Greek and Roman readers.

fuentes/antiguedades-judias/por_que_impo.texto: It is the main source on the Hasmoneans and Herod; it mentions John the Baptist, James “the brother of Jesus” and, in a passage altered by Christian copyists, Jesus.

fuentes/antiguedades-judias/leer.0.titul.texto: English translation by William Whiston (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/mapa-de-madaba/soporte.texto: Mosaic on the floor of a church

fuentes/mapa-de-madaba/resumen.texto: Mosaic map of the Holy Land and the Nile Delta, with Jerusalem at the center, its colonnaded street and the Holy Sepulchre.

fuentes/mapa-de-madaba/por_que_importa.texto: It is the oldest surviving map of the region and was used to excavate Byzantine Jerusalem.

fuentes/itinerario-de-burdeos/resumen.texto: List of the stages of a pilgrim's journey from Bordeaux to Jerusalem and back, with brief notes on the holy places and the basilica Constantine was building at the Holy Sepulchre.

fuentes/itinerario-de-burdeos/por_que_im.texto: It is the oldest surviving account of a Christian pilgrimage.

fuentes/peregrinacion-de-egeria/resumen.texto: Account of a journey to Sinai, Jerusalem, Egypt and Mesopotamia, with a detailed description of the liturgy of Jerusalem throughout the year.

fuentes/peregrinacion-de-egeria/por_que_.texto: It is a unique source on 4th-century Christian Jerusalem and on spoken Latin.

fuentes/onomasticon/resumen.texto: Dictionary of the places of the Bible, with their names and their location in Roman Palestine, which Jerome translated into Latin.

fuentes/historia-eclesiastica-de-eusebio.texto: The first history of the Church, from Jesus to Constantine, with quotations from many documents now lost.

fuentes/vida-de-constantino/resumen.texto: Laudatory biography of the first Christian emperor, with the account of the building of the Holy Sepulchre and the emperor's letter to the bishop of Jerusalem.

fuentes/doctrina-jacobi/resumen.texto: Dialogue in which a Jew forcibly baptized under Heraclius debates with other Jews. It quotes a letter from Palestine according to which a prophet has appeared among the Saracens who announces the messiah and “comes armed with a sword”; a Jew remarks that prophets do not come with a sword.

fuentes/doctrina-jacobi/por_que_importa.texto: It is the oldest text that mentions Muhammad, written in the lifetime of his companions.

fuentes/historia-de-sebeos/resumen.texto: Armenian chronicle of the wars between Byzantium and Persia and of the Arab conquests, with an account of how Muhammad preached to the Arabs the faith of the God of Abraham and launched them to conquer the land promised to their ancestor.

fuentes/historia-de-sebeos/por_que_impor.texto: It is the oldest and most detailed non-Muslim narrative of the origin of Islam.

fuentes/cronica-de-juan-de-nikiu/resumen.texto: Universal chronicle by a Coptic bishop that narrates the Arab conquest of Egypt, with its violence, the tribute and the collaboration of part of the local population.

fuentes/apocalipsis-del-pseudo-metodio/r.texto: Prophecy attributed to a 4th-century martyr: Arab rule is a punishment for the sins of the Christians, but a Roman emperor will defeat the “sons of Ishmael” and lay down his crown in Jerusalem.

fuentes/apocalipsis-del-pseudo-metodio/p.texto: Translated into Greek and Latin, it was one of the most widely read apocalyptic texts of the Middle Ages and fed the image of the “Last Emperor” who would recover Jerusalem.

fuentes/sermon-de-navidad-de-sofronio/re.texto: Homily by the patriarch of Jerusalem lamenting that the “Saracen sword” prevents the faithful from going to Bethlehem, like Adam expelled from paradise, and attributing it to the sins of the Christians.

fuentes/sermon-de-navidad-de-sofronio/po.texto: It is a direct testimony of the Arab invasion of Palestine.

fuentes/pacto-de-omar/resumen.texto: Text in the form of a letter from the Christians of a Syrian city to the caliph: they undertake not to build new churches, not to display crosses or ring bells loudly, to dress differently from Muslims, to give up their seats to them and not to prevent their own people from converting, in exchange for protection (dhimma).

fuentes/pacto-de-omar/por_que_importa.texto: It was the model for the restrictions on Jews and Christians (dhimmis) in Islamic law. Its attribution to Umar I is doubtful: many historians place it in the time of Umar II (717–720) or later.

fuentes/dialogo-de-timoteo-i/autor.texto: Timothy I, patriarch of the Church of the East

fuentes/dialogo-de-timoteo-i/resumen.texto: Account of two days of courteous debate between the Nestorian patriarch and the Abbasid caliph on the Trinity, the incarnation and the prophethood of Muhammad, of whom the patriarch concedes that he “walked in the path of the prophets”.

fuentes/dialogo-de-timoteo-i/por_que_imp.texto: It is a classic text of dialogue between Christians and Muslims.

fuentes/cronografia-de-teofanes/resumen.texto: Year-by-year chronicle of the Empire from 284 to 813, with the Arab conquests, the sieges of Constantinople and a hostile biography of Muhammad.

fuentes/conquistas-de-los-paises/titulo.texto: Book of the Conquests of the Lands

fuentes/conquistas-de-los-paises/resumen.texto: History of the Arab conquests region by region, with the surrender treaties of each city and the terms of the tribute.

fuentes/conquistas-de-los-paises/por_que.texto: It is the best Arabic source on how the conquered territories were organized.

fuentes/historia-de-al-tabari/titulo.texto: History of the Prophets and Kings

fuentes/historia-de-al-tabari/resumen.texto: Universal history from the creation to 915, which records, with their transmitters, every version of each event the author found.

fuentes/ciudad-virtuosa/resumen.texto: Treatise that moves from God and the cosmos to the human soul and the perfect city, governed by a ruler who is both philosopher and prophet, and describes the ignorant and errant cities.

fuentes/ciudad-virtuosa/por_que_importa.texto: It joined Plato's Republic with Islamic theology and influenced Avicenna, Averroes and Maimonides.

fuentes/descripcion-de-las-regiones/titu.texto: The Best Divisions for Knowledge of the Regions

fuentes/descripcion-de-las-regiones/resu.texto: Geography of the Islamic world by province, based on the author's own travels, with climate, customs, coinage, trade and languages.

fuentes/descripcion-de-las-regiones/por_.texto: Its description of Jerusalem and Palestine in the 10th century, with a native's pride and complaints about the lack of scholars, is unique.

fuentes/safarnama/resumen.texto: Account of seven years of travel from Persia to Cairo and Mecca, with the description of Jerusalem in 1047, its sacred esplanade and the Muslim pilgrims who went there instead of to Mecca.

fuentes/incoherencia-de-los-filosofos/re.texto: Attack on twenty theses of the Aristotelian philosophers, above all Avicenna, such as the eternity of the world, that God does not know particulars, or the denial of bodily resurrection; it holds that the link between cause and effect depends on the will of God.

fuentes/incoherencia-de-los-filosofos/po.texto: Averroes replied to it with The Incoherence of the Incoherence; it is a landmark in the relationship between philosophy and theology in Islam.

fuentes/libro-del-yihad/resumen.texto: Lectures delivered in public in Damascus calling on the Muslims of Syria to wage jihad against the Franks. It explains their arrival as part of a Christian offensive that had already taken Sicily and part of al-Andalus from them, and attributes the defeat to the division of the princes and the abandonment of religion.

fuentes/libro-del-yihad/por_que_importa.texto: It is the first Muslim call to jihad against the crusaders and anticipates the program of Nur al-Din and Saladin.

fuentes/cronica-de-damasco/titulo.texto: Continuation of the History of Damascus

fuentes/cronica-de-damasco/resumen.texto: Chronicle of Damascus from the 11th century to 1160, covering the arrival of the Franks, the fall of Jerusalem and the Second Crusade's attack on the city.

fuentes/libro-de-las-ensenanzas/resumen.texto: Memoirs of a warrior emir, hunter and poet, dictated at the age of ninety: battles, hunts and anecdotes about the Franks, brave but barbarous in their medicine, their ordeals and their customs. He distinguishes newcomers from those who had lived in the East for some time, and recounts that the Templars defended him from a Frank who would not let him pray toward Mecca.

fuentes/libro-de-las-ensenanzas/por_que_.texto: It is the most personal Muslim view of the crusaders.

fuentes/libro-de-las-ensenanzas/leer.0.t.texto: Passages on the Franks, English translation (Medieval Sourcebook, Fordham)

fuentes/historia-de-damasco/resumen.texto: Enormous biographical dictionary of all the figures connected with Damascus since the conquest, supported by Nur al-Din.

fuentes/conquista-de-jerusalen-imad/resu.texto: Account of Hattin and of Saladin's capture of Jerusalem in rhymed prose, with the purification of the Dome of the Rock and al-Aqsa and the first Friday prayer.

fuentes/vida-de-saladino/resumen.texto: Biography of Saladin by the judge of his army, who portrays him as pious, generous and devoted to jihad; he narrates as an eyewitness the siege of Acre and the massacre of Ayyadieh.

fuentes/historia-completa/resumen.texto: Universal history up to 1231 with the most complete Muslim account of the crusades and of the Mongol invasion, which it calls the greatest catastrophe in history.

fuentes/historia-completa/por_que_import.texto: It presents the First Crusade as part of a Frankish offensive that had begun in Toledo and Sicily, and criticizes the divisions among the Muslim princes.

fuentes/historia-de-abulfeda/resumen.texto: Universal history up to 1329, with the author's testimony on the capture of Acre in 1291. Translated into Latin in the 18th century, it was a source on Muhammad for European orientalists.

fuentes/fatuas-de-ibn-taymiyya/resumen.texto: Rulings declaring it obligatory to fight the Mongols of the Ilkhanate even though they had converted to Islam, because they governed according to Mongol law and not according to Islamic law.

fuentes/fatuas-de-ibn-taymiyya/por_que_i.texto: His arguments on jihad against rulers who claim to be Muslim were taken up by Sayyid Qutb, the group that killed Sadat, and al-Qaeda.

fuentes/rihla/resumen.texto: Account of almost thirty years of travels, from the Maghreb to China, dictated in Fez to the secretary Ibn Juzayy.

fuentes/muqaddima/resumen.texto: Introduction to his universal history: a theory of society, power and the economy in which dynasties arise from the group cohesion (asabiyya) of desert peoples and weaken within three or four generations of urban life. It opens with a critique of historians' errors.

fuentes/muqaddima/por_que_importa.texto: It is regarded as a forerunner of sociology and of the philosophy of history.

fuentes/historia-de-jerusalen-y-hebron/t.texto: The Glorious History of Jerusalem and Hebron

fuentes/historia-de-jerusalen-y-hebron/r.texto: History and description of the two holy cities of Palestine, from the biblical prophets to the Mamluks, with their mosques, madrasas and scholars.

fuentes/discurso-de-clermont/titulo.texto: Speech of Urban II at Clermont

fuentes/discurso-de-clermont/resumen.texto: The pope called on knights to aid the Christians of the East and to liberate Jerusalem, with the promise of the remission of sins. The text has not survived: there are five versions by chroniclers (Fulcher of Chartres, Robert the Monk, Baldric of Dol, Guibert of Nogent and the Deeds of the Franks), written after the capture of Jerusalem and very different from one another.

fuentes/discurso-de-clermont/por_que_imp.texto: It is the founding act of the crusades. Robert the Monk's version describes in graphic terms the atrocities attributed to the Turks and puts in the mouth of the crowd the cry “God wills it!”.

fuentes/discurso-de-clermont/leer.0.titu.texto: The five versions of the speech, in English (Medieval Sourcebook, Fordham)

fuentes/carta-de-alejo-a-roberto-de-flan.texto: Letter of Alexios I to Robert of Flanders

Letter in which the emperor begs the count of Flanders and the princes of the West to come and save Constantinople from the Turks and the Pechenegs, with descriptions of atrocities against Christians and the lure of the city's relics and riches.
Most historians consider it a forgery or a Latin reworking, perhaps based on a genuine letter of Alexios, used as crusade propaganda. The authentic request for help is that of the envoys at Piacenza.

fuentes/cronica-de-bernoldo/resumen.texto: Chronicle by a monk who supported the Gregorian reform. It records that in March 1095 an embassy from the emperor of Constantinople came to the council of Piacenza and begged the pope and the faithful for help against the pagans who had advanced almost to the walls of the city.

fuentes/cronica-de-bernoldo/por_que_impo.texto: It is the contemporary testimony of the Byzantine request that preceded the First Crusade.

fuentes/historia-hierosolymitana/resumen.texto: Chronicle of the First Crusade and of the first kings of Jerusalem written by an eyewitness, with a version of the speech at Clermont and the famous reflection: “we who were Westerners have become Easterners”.

fuentes/historia-de-raimundo-de-aguilers.texto: History of the Franks Who Captured Jerusalem

Chronicle by the chaplain of Raymond of Toulouse, with the discovery of the Holy Lance at Antioch and the capture of Jerusalem, where, he writes, in the portico of the Temple of Solomon the crusaders rode in blood up to their knees and the horses' bridles, “a just judgment of God”.

fuentes/historia-de-alberto-de-aquisgran.texto: History of the Expedition to Jerusalem
The most detailed chronicle of the First Crusade and of the early years of the kingdom, written from veterans' accounts; it recounts the People's Crusade and condemns Emicho's massacres of Jews.

fuentes/gesta-dei-per-francos/titulo.texto: The Deeds of God through the Franks

fuentes/gesta-dei-per-francos/resumen.texto: Theological rewriting of the First Crusade, which presents it as a new form of salvation for laypeople without leaving the world. It includes a legendary and defamatory life of Muhammad.

fuentes/historia-de-guillermo-de-tiro/ti.texto: History of Deeds Done Beyond the Sea

fuentes/historia-de-guillermo-de-tiro/re.texto: History of the Kingdom of Jerusalem written by its chancellor using documents and Arabic sources; it describes the kingdom's decline and portrays Nur al-Din and Saladin with respect.

fuentes/historia-de-guillermo-de-tiro/po.texto: Translated and continued in French, it was for centuries the reference work on the crusades.

fuentes/cronica-de-salomon-bar-simson/re.texto: The longest of the Hebrew chronicles of 1096: it narrates the crusaders' attacks on Speyer, Worms and Mainz, the resistance, the martyrdom (kiddush hashem) of entire families who took their own lives before they could be baptized, and the conduct of the bishops.

fuentes/cronica-de-salomon-bar-simson/po.texto: It is the Jewish voice of the First Crusade.

fuentes/cronica-de-salomon-bar-simson/le.texto: “The Crusaders in Mainz”, English translation (Medieval Sourcebook, Fordham)

fuentes/cronica-de-mateo-de-edesa/resume.texto: Chronicle by an Armenian monk on the Turkish invasions, the arrival of the crusaders and the Frankish County of Edessa, whom he views first with hope and then with bitterness.

fuentes/cronica-de-miguel-el-sirio/autor.texto: Michael the Syrian, Syriac Orthodox patriarch

fuentes/cronica-de-miguel-el-sirio/resum.texto: Universal chronicle by the patriarch of the Syriac Orthodox Church, with the view of Eastern Christians on Arabs, Byzantines, Turks and crusaders.

fuentes/cronografia-de-bar-hebreo/resume.texto: Universal history by a Syriac bishop and polymath who lived under the Mongols; it narrates the crusades and the fall of Baghdad.

fuentes/elogio-de-la-nueva-milicia/titul.texto: In Praise of the New Knighthood

fuentes/elogio-de-la-nueva-milicia/resum.texto: Treatise addressed to Hugh of Payns justifying the Order of the Temple: the knight of Christ who kills an evildoer commits not homicide but “malicide”, and if he dies he is a martyr. It ends with a spiritual pilgrimage through the holy places.

fuentes/elogio-de-la-nueva-milicia/por_q.texto: It gave the Latin Church the theology of the warrior monk. Bernard himself, when preaching the Second Crusade, forbade attacks on Jews and went to the Rhineland to stop the massacres.

fuentes/regla-del-temple/resumen.texto: Rule approved at the Council of Troyes and inspired by that of the Cistercians: prayer, poverty, obedience and war for the knights of the Temple.

fuentes/quantum-praedecessores/resumen.texto: Bull calling the Second Crusade after the fall of Edessa, recalling the example of the First and setting out the crusaders' privileges: remission of sins, protection of family and property, and suspension of debts.

fuentes/itinerario-de-ricardo/titulo.texto: Itinerary of the Pilgrims and Deeds of King Richard

fuentes/itinerario-de-ricardo/autor.texto: Attributed to Richard of Holy Trinity

fuentes/itinerario-de-ricardo/resumen.texto: Chronicle of the Third Crusade centered on Richard the Lionheart: the conquest of Cyprus, the siege of Acre, Arsuf and the truce with Saladin.

fuentes/quia-maior/resumen.texto: Bull calling the Fifth Crusade and extending the indulgence to those who only paid for it; it identifies Muhammad with the beast of the Apocalypse and announces that his power is nearing its end.

fuentes/historia-de-nicetas-coniates/res.texto: History of Byzantium from 1118 to 1207, with the sack of Constantinople by the crusaders in 1204: the desecration of Hagia Sophia, the melting down of ancient statues and the comparison with Saladin's clemency in Jerusalem.

fuentes/historia-de-nicetas-coniates/por.texto: It is the Greek voice of the Fourth Crusade; the resentment it expresses weighed in the failure of all the unions of the Churches.

fuentes/historia-de-nicetas-coniates/lee.texto: The sack of 1204, English translation (Medieval Sourcebook, Fordham)

fuentes/libro-de-viajes-de-benjamin/resu.texto: Account of the journey through the Jewish communities from Navarre to Baghdad and Egypt, with figures for families, trades and monuments; it describes crusader Jerusalem and the Tomb of the Patriarchs in Hebron.

fuentes/libro-de-viajes-de-benjamin/leer.texto: English translation by Marcus Nathan Adler (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/cartas-de-federico-ii/titulo.texto: Letters of the Crusade of Frederick II

fuentes/cartas-de-federico-ii/resumen.texto: Letters by the emperor and his critics on the handover of Jerusalem by treaty: Frederick presents the agreement as a triumph; the patriarch of Jerusalem, as a betrayal that left the Temple Mount to the Muslims.

fuentes/lex-mahumet/titulo.texto: The Law of Muhammad the Pseudo-Prophet

fuentes/lex-mahumet/resumen.texto: First Latin translation of the Quran, a loose paraphrase made in Spain for Peter the Venerable as part of a collection of texts on Islam (the Toledan Collection).

fuentes/lex-mahumet/por_que_importa.texto: It was the form in which Europe read the Quran until the 17th century; Bibliander printed it in 1543.

fuentes/contra-sectam-sarracenorum/titul.texto: Against the Sect of the Saracens

fuentes/contra-sectam-sarracenorum/resum.texto: Refutation of Islam addressed to the Muslims themselves, whom he invites to debate: “I love you; loving you, I write to you; writing to you, I invite you to salvation”.

fuentes/contra-sectam-sarracenorum/por_q.texto: It is the first Latin work that attempts to argue with Islam on the basis of its texts and not only of legends.

fuentes/contra-legem-sarracenorum/titulo.texto: Against the Law of the Saracens

fuentes/contra-legem-sarracenorum/resume.texto: Refutation of the Quran based on his reading of it in Arabic in Baghdad. In another work, his letters to the Church triumphant, Riccoldo himself admires the prayer, hospitality and devotion of Muslims, which put Christians to shame.

fuentes/contra-legem-sarracenorum/por_qu.texto: Translated into Greek by Demetrios Kydones and into German by Luther, it was the basis of European polemic against Islam until the early modern period.

fuentes/opus-tripartitum/resumen.texto: Memorandum for the Council of Lyon defending the crusade against its critics—those who said that Christians should not shed blood, that God did not favor it, or that it was better to convert than to kill—and proposing to reform the Church and unite it with the Greeks.

fuentes/opus-tripartitum/por_que_importa.texto: It shows that by the late 13th century the crusade was being debated within Europe itself.

fuentes/de-recuperatione-terrae-sanctae/.texto: On the Recovery of the Holy Land

Plan to recover the Holy Land that is in fact a program for Europe: peace among Christians under a council and an arbitration tribunal, confiscation of Church property, colonies in the East and schools of Arabic and Greek, also for women.
It is cited as a precursor of ideas of European federation.

fuentes/liber-secretorum/titulo.texto: Book of the Secrets of the Faithful of the Cross

fuentes/liber-secretorum/resumen.texto: Crusade plan based on a trade blockade of Egypt and a standing fleet, with maps by Pietro Vesconte of the Holy Land, the Mediterranean and the world.

fuentes/dialogos-con-un-persa/resumen.texto: Twenty-six dialogues with a Muslim scholar (a mudarris) in Ankara, during the winter when the emperor was serving as a vassal in Sultan Bayezid's campaign. They discuss the prophets, the law and reason; Manuel argues that acting with violence is contrary to the nature of God.

fuentes/dialogos-con-un-persa/por_que_im.texto: Benedict XVI quoted one of its harshest passages on Muhammad in Regensburg (2006), which provoked a crisis and later a dialogue with Muslim scholars.

fuentes/apologias-de-cantacuceno/resumen.texto: Four apologies for Christianity and four discourses against Muhammad written by the retired emperor as a monk, at the request of a convert from Islam.

fuentes/cribratio-alkorani/resumen.texto: Reading of the Quran that seeks in it, “as in a sieve”, the Christian truths it would contain, such as the Trinity and the divinity of Christ, in order to show them to Muslims.

fuentes/cribratio-alkorani/por_que_impor.texto: Together with On the Peace of Faith, it is the most conciliatory response by a European philosopher to the fall of Constantinople.

fuentes/carta-a-mehmed/resumen.texto: Letter from the pope to the sultan, probably never sent, inviting him to be baptized in order to be recognized as the greatest emperor in the world, with a long comparison between Christianity and Islam.

fuentes/historia-de-critobulo/resumen.texto: History of the first seventeen years of the reign of Mehmed II, including the capture of Constantinople, written by a Greek in his service.

fuentes/historia-de-ducas/resumen.texto: History of the fall of Byzantium to the Ottomans, with the most dramatic account of the siege and sack of 1453.

fuentes/cronica-de-esfrantzes/resumen.texto: Memoirs of the last emperor's friend: the defense of Constantinople, the death of Constantine XI and the enslavement of his own family.

fuentes/diario-de-barbaro/titulo.texto: Diary of the Siege of Constantinople

fuentes/diario-de-barbaro/resumen.texto: Day-by-day diary of the siege, written by a physician of the Venetian galleys, with the list of Venetians killed and captured.

fuentes/evagatorium/resumen.texto: Enormous account of the two pilgrimages of a Dominican from Ulm to Jerusalem, Sinai and Cairo under the Mamluks, with the pilgrims, the guides, the Franciscans of Mount Zion and the Muslims.

fuentes/sobre-la-guerra-contra-el-turco/.texto: Treatise published months before the siege of Vienna: war against the Turks is legitimate as defense, but it must be waged by the emperor by virtue of his office and not by the pope as a crusade; the Turk is a rod with which God punishes Christendom.

fuentes/coran-de-bibliander/resumen.texto: First printed edition of the Quran in Europe, with Robert of Ketton's translation and polemical texts, published after a dispute with the Basel city council, which had jailed the printer; Luther wrote a preface.

fuentes/jerusalen-liberada/resumen.texto: Epic poem on the First Crusade and the capture of Jerusalem, with Godfrey, Tancred and Rinaldo, love affairs with Muslim warrior women and sorceresses such as Clorinda and Armida, and battles between angels and demons.

fuentes/jerusalen-liberada/por_que_impor.texto: It fixed the literary image of the crusades in Europe and inspired operas, paintings and ballets for two centuries.

fuentes/jerusalen-liberada/leer.1.titulo.texto: English translation by Edward Fairfax (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/mahoma-o-el-fanatismo/resumen.texto: Tragedy in which Muhammad, portrayed as an ambitious impostor, manipulates a young man into killing his own father.

fuentes/mahoma-o-el-fanatismo/por_que_im.texto: Through Islam Voltaire was attacking all fanaticism, Christian fanaticism included; he dedicated the play to Pope Benedict XIV. Later, in the Essay on Customs, he gave a more nuanced image of Muhammad and of the crusades.

fuentes/natan-el-sabio/resumen.texto: Drama set in Jerusalem during the truce of the Third Crusade. Saladin asks the Jew Nathan which religion is the true one, and Nathan replies with the parable of the three rings that no one can tell apart.

fuentes/natan-el-sabio/por_que_importa.texto: It is the great Enlightenment plea for tolerance among Jews, Christians and Muslims; the Nazis banned it.

fuentes/decadencia-y-caida/titulo.texto: The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire

fuentes/decadencia-y-caida/resumen.texto: History of Rome and Byzantium up to 1453 in six volumes; chapters 50 to 52 deal with Muhammad and the Arab conquests, and chapters 58 to 61 with the crusades.

fuentes/decadencia-y-caida/por_que_impor.texto: Its irony about Christian fanaticism and its relative admiration for Muhammad shaped the Enlightenment view of Islam and of the crusades.

fuentes/decadencia-y-caida/leer.1.titulo.texto: Volume V, with the chapters on Muhammad and the Arab conquests (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/viaje-por-siria-y-egipto/resumen.texto: Systematic, unromantic description of the geography, population and government of Syria, Palestine and Egypt under the Ottomans and the Mamluks.

fuentes/divan-de-oriente-y-occidente/res.texto: Collection of poems inspired by the Persian poet Hafez, with notes on the history and culture of the East.

fuentes/divan-de-oriente-y-occidente/por.texto: It proposes a dialogue between European and Islamic poetry; it gave its name to the orchestra of young Israeli and Arab musicians founded by Daniel Barenboim and Edward Said in 1999.

fuentes/itinerario-de-paris-a-jerusalen/.texto: Account of the 1806–1807 journey through Greece, Constantinople, Jerusalem, Egypt and Tunis, with a defense of the crusades as a struggle of Christian civilization against an Islam he presents as an enemy of freedom.

fuentes/el-talisman/resumen.texto: Novel of the Third Crusade in which Saladin, disguised as a physician, heals Richard the Lionheart and proves nobler than many crusaders.

fuentes/viaje-a-oriente/resumen.texto: Memories and impressions of a journey through Lebanon, Palestine and Syria, with religious meditations in Jerusalem and a romantic view of the East.

fuentes/el-heroe-como-profeta/resumen.texto: Lectures on great men; the second, “The Hero as Prophet”, defends Muhammad's sincerity against the European tradition that portrayed him as an impostor.

fuentes/vida-de-jesus/resumen.texto: Biography of Jesus as a man, without miracles, written after a journey through Galilee; it was both a scandal and a great success.

fuentes/el-islam-y-la-ciencia/resumen.texto: Lecture at the Sorbonne arguing that Islam was always hostile to science and philosophy, and that so-called Arab science was the work of Persians, Christians and Jews in spite of Islam.

fuentes/el-islam-y-la-ciencia/por_que_im.texto: It provoked al-Afghani's reply and is a key text in the debate on Islam and modernity.

fuentes/respuesta-a-renan/resumen.texto: Letter published in the Journal des Débats: Islam, like Christianity in its time, held back science and philosophy, but Muslim peoples can free themselves from that tutelage as Europe did.

fuentes/inocentes-en-el-extranjero/resum.texto: Humorous account of the 1867 cruise of American pilgrims to Europe and the Holy Land, which describes a poor and desolate Palestine and mocks the relics, the guides and the pilgrims themselves.

fuentes/inocentes-en-el-extranjero/por_q.texto: It was the best-selling travel book of its time; its descriptions of Palestine are cited, to opposite ends, in the debate over the region's population in the 19th century.

fuentes/survey-of-western-palestine/auto.texto: Palestine Exploration Fund (Conder, Kitchener and others)

fuentes/survey-of-western-palestine/resu.texto: Map of Palestine west of the Jordan at a scale of one inch to the mile, with thousands of Arabic place names and descriptions of ruins and villages, surveyed between 1871 and 1877.

fuentes/survey-of-western-palestine/por_.texto: It was the basis of the region's cartography for half a century and is a source on its villages before Zionism.

fuentes/epistola-a-yemen/resumen.texto: Letter to the Jews of Yemen, persecuted by a ruler who wanted to convert them and confused by a false messiah. Maimonides consoles them, asks them to be prudent and writes that no nation has oppressed Israel as much as the nation of Ishmael.

fuentes/epistola-a-yemen/por_que_importa.texto: It is a key text on the condition of Jews under Islam and on Jewish messianism.

fuentes/carta-de-najmanides/resumen.texto: Letter from the rabbi of Girona, exiled after the Disputation of Barcelona, to his son: he found Jerusalem devastated after the passage of the Mongols, with only two Jewish families, and reopened a synagogue in a ruined house.

fuentes/carta-de-najmanides/por_que_impo.texto: The Ramban Synagogue, in the Old City, is considered the oldest of those still active in Jerusalem.

fuentes/odas-a-sion/resumen.texto: Poems of longing for Jerusalem by the great poet of al-Andalus: “My heart is in the East, and I am at the far end of the West”. Halevi set out for the Holy Land in 1140 and died shortly afterwards.

fuentes/odas-a-sion/por_que_importa.texto: They are the classic texts of Jewish love for Zion and are still recited in the liturgy of Tisha B'Av.

fuentes/cartas-de-bertinoro/resumen.texto: Letters to his father and his brother about the journey through Egypt and the life of the Jews of Jerusalem under the Mamluks: poverty, taxes and disputes within the community.

fuentes/leja-dodi/resumen.texto: Hymn of the Safed kabbalists for welcoming the Sabbath as a bride, with images of the restoration of Jerusalem.

fuentes/shulchan-aruj/resumen.texto: Code of Jewish law in four parts, written in Safed and printed in Venice in 1565. With the Ashkenazi glosses of Moses Isserles, it remains the standard of Orthodox Jewish practice.

fuentes/arbol-de-la-vida/resumen.texto: Exposition of the Kabbalah of Isaac Luria: God's contraction to make room for the world, the breaking of the vessels meant to hold his light, and the repair of the world through human deeds.

fuentes/roma-y-jerusalen/resumen.texto: Essay that, inspired by Italian unification, calls for a nation of their own for the Jews in Palestine, socialist and agricultural, because German antisemitism would not disappear through assimilation.

fuentes/autoemancipacion/resumen.texto: Pamphlet written after the pogroms of 1881: Judeophobia is an incurable disease of the nations, and the Jews will only be respected when they have a territory of their own.

fuentes/la-verdad-desde-la-tierra-de-isr.texto: Truth from the Land of Israel
Report after a journey to the colonies: the land is not empty, the Arabs understand what is happening and will one day resist, and the settlers must treat them with respect and justice.

fuentes/el-estado-judio/resumen.texto: Proposal for a Jewish state recognized by the powers, organized by a Society of Jews and a Jewish Company. Herzl asks “Palestine or Argentina?”: Argentina, where Baron Hirsch's colonies already existed, was the alternative.

fuentes/el-estado-judio/por_que_importa.texto: It is the founding text of political Zionism.

fuentes/programa-de-basilea/resumen.texto: Declaration of the First Zionist Congress: “Zionism aims at the creation of a home for the Jewish people in Palestine secured by public law”, through Jewish colonization, organization and national consciousness.

fuentes/protocolos-de-los-sabios-de-sion.texto: The Protocols of the Elders of Zion

Purported minutes of a secret meeting of Jewish leaders plotting to dominate the world, published in Russia in 1903. They are a forgery: in 1921 The Times showed that they copied a pamphlet by Maurice Joly against Napoleon III that did not mention the Jews.

It was the most widely distributed antisemitic book of the 20th century: Nazi propaganda used it, and from the mid-century it circulated widely in the Arab world. The Hamas Charter cites it in its Article 32.

fuentes/despertar-de-la-nacion-arabe/tit.texto: The Awakening of the Arab Nation

fuentes/despertar-de-la-nacion-arabe/res.texto: Manifesto for an Arab empire independent of the Turks, warning that the Arab awakening and the Jewish effort to reconstitute the ancient kingdom of Israel are destined to fight each other until one defeats the other.

fuentes/correspondencia-husein-mcmahon/a.texto: Hussein ibn Ali and Henry McMahon

fuentes/correspondencia-husein-mcmahon/r.texto: Ten letters between the Sharif of Mecca and the British High Commissioner in Egypt: Britain promises to recognize Arab independence in exchange for a revolt against the Ottomans, with ambiguous territorial exclusions.

fuentes/correspondencia-husein-mcmahon/p.texto: Arabs and the British argued for decades over whether Palestine was included in the promise.

fuentes/correspondencia-husein-mcmahon/l.texto: The letters, in English, on Wikisource
Letter of 24 October 1915 (Modern History Sourcebook, Fordham)

fuentes/acuerdo-sykes-picot/resumen.texto: Secret agreement between Britain and France, with Russian consent, to divide the Arab provinces of the Ottoman Empire between them, with Palestine under international administration. The Bolsheviks published it in 1917.

fuentes/acuerdo-sykes-picot/leer.0.titul.texto: English text (Avalon Project, Yale Law School)

fuentes/declaracion-balfour/resumen.texto: Letter from the British Foreign Secretary to Lord Rothschild: the government views with favour “the establishment in Palestine of a national home for the Jewish people”, without prejudice to the civil and religious rights of non-Jewish communities or to the rights of Jews in other countries.

fuentes/acuerdo-faisal-weizmann/autor.texto: Faisal ibn Hussein and Chaim Weizmann

fuentes/acuerdo-faisal-weizmann/resumen.texto: Cooperation agreement between Emir Faisal and the Zionist leader: acceptance of Jewish immigration to Palestine and protection of Arab peasants, made conditional by Faisal, in a handwritten note, on the promised Arab independence, which never came.

fuentes/informe-king-crane/resumen.texto: Report of an American commission that consulted the population of Syria and Palestine: the great majority rejected the Zionist program and called for a united and independent Syria. It was shelved without effect.

fuentes/mandato-para-palestina/resumen.texto: Text that entrusted Palestine to Britain and incorporated the Balfour Declaration, with a Jewish agency for immigration and settlement; one article allowed Transjordan to be excluded from the Jewish national home.

fuentes/libro-blanco-de-1922/resumen.texto: Official interpretation of the Balfour Declaration: the Jewish national home did not mean turning all of Palestine Jewish, and immigration would depend on the country's economic capacity.

fuentes/el-muro-de-hierro/resumen.texto: Article arguing that no native people voluntarily accepts colonization and that the Arabs of Palestine would be no exception: Zionism could only advance behind an “iron wall” of Jewish force that would bring them to negotiate.

fuentes/informe-peel/titulo.texto: Report of the Palestine Royal Commission (Peel Report)

fuentes/informe-peel/resumen.texto: Report of some 400 pages on the causes of the Arab revolt of 1936: “an irrepressible conflict has arisen between two national communities within the narrow bounds of one small country”. It proposes dividing Palestine into a Jewish state in Galilee and the coastal plain, an Arab state united with Transjordan, and a permanent British mandate over Jerusalem, Bethlehem and a corridor to Jaffa, with population transfers.

fuentes/informe-peel/por_que_importa.texto: It was the first official partition proposal. The Arab leaders rejected it; the Zionist Congress accepted it as a basis for negotiation, and the British government abandoned it in 1938.

fuentes/informe-peel/leer.0.titulo.texto: The full report in PDF (UNISPAL, United Nations)

fuentes/libro-blanco-de-1939/resumen.texto: New British policy: an independent Palestinian state within ten years, Jewish immigration limited to 75,000 people over five years and thereafter subject to Arab consent, and restrictions on land sales to Jews.

fuentes/libro-blanco-de-1939/por_que_imp.texto: It closed Palestine to Jews fleeing Europe on the eve of the Holocaust. The Zionists fought it, and the Arab Higher Committee also rejected it.

fuentes/programa-de-biltmore/resumen.texto: Resolution of the Zionists gathered at the Biltmore Hotel in New York: Palestine was to be established as a “Jewish Commonwealth” open to immigration, and not as a home within an Arab state.

fuentes/pacto-de-la-liga-arabe/autor.texto: Egypt, Iraq, Transjordan, Syria, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia and Yemen

fuentes/pacto-de-la-liga-arabe/resumen.texto: Founding treaty of the League of Arab States, with an annex affirming the existence of Palestine as an independent state and the participation of its Arab representatives in the League.

fuentes/resolucion-181/resumen.texto: Plan for the partition of Palestine into an Arab state and a Jewish state joined by an economic union, with Jerusalem and Bethlehem under a special international regime (corpus separatum).

fuentes/declaracion-de-independencia-de-.texto: People's Council, read by David Ben-Gurion

Proclamation of the State of Israel that invokes the history of the Jewish people in its land, the Holocaust and Resolution 181; it promises “complete equality of social and political rights to all its inhabitants irrespective of religion, race or sex” and extends the hand of peace to neighbouring states.

fuentes/resolucion-194/resumen.texto: Establishes the Conciliation Commission for Palestine and states, in its paragraph 11, that refugees wishing to live at peace with their neighbours should be permitted to return at the earliest practicable date, and that those choosing not to return should be compensated.

fuentes/resolucion-194/por_que_importa.texto: It is the basis of the Palestinian claim to the “right of return”.

fuentes/acuerdos-de-armisticio/autor.texto: Israel, Egypt, Lebanon, Jordan and Syria

fuentes/acuerdos-de-armisticio/resumen.texto: Four agreements signed between February and July 1949 with the mediation of Ralph Bunche, which set armistice lines, the “Green Line”, without the status of definitive borders.

fuentes/carta-nacional-palestina/resumen.texto: Founding document of the PLO (1964), revised in 1968: Palestine, within the borders of the Mandate, is an indivisible unit; armed struggle is the only way to liberate it; the 1947 partition and the Balfour Declaration are null and void, and only Jews who lived in Palestine before the “Zionist invasion” are considered Palestinians.

fuentes/carta-nacional-palestina/por_que.texto: Arafat declared it “caduc” (lapsed) in 1989, and the National Council voted in 1996 and 1998 to annul the articles contrary to the recognition of Israel.

fuentes/carta-nacional-palestina/leer.0..texto: English translation of the 1968 version (Avalon Project, Yale)

fuentes/resolucion-de-jartum/resumen.texto: Declaration of the Arab summit following the Six-Day War: unity to eliminate the effects of the aggression and “no peace with Israel, no recognition of Israel, no negotiations with it”.

fuentes/resolucion-242/resumen.texto: “Land for peace” formula: withdrawal of Israel from territories occupied in the conflict, an end to belligerency and recognition of the right of every state to live in peace within secure boundaries; it calls for a just settlement of the refugee problem.

fuentes/resolucion-242/por_que_importa.texto: The absence of the article in the English version (“from territories”, not “from the territories”) fuelled a decades-long debate over whether it required full withdrawal.

fuentes/acuerdos-de-camp-david/autor.texto: Anwar Sadat, Menachem Begin and Jimmy Carter

fuentes/acuerdos-de-camp-david/resumen.texto: Two frameworks signed after thirteen days of negotiation: one for peace between Egypt and Israel, with the return of the Sinai, and another for a five-year Palestinian autonomy in the West Bank and Gaza.

fuentes/tratado-de-paz-egipto-israel/res.texto: End of the state of war, mutual recognition, Israeli withdrawal from the Sinai within three years and free Israeli passage through the Suez Canal.

fuentes/carta-de-hamas/resumen.texto: Founding charter of Hamas, published on 18 August 1988, in 36 articles. It defines Hamas as the branch of the Muslim Brotherhood in Palestine; declares that Palestine is an Islamic waqf (religious endowment) of which no part may be ceded (Art. 11), and rejects negotiations and peace conferences: “there is no solution for the Palestinian question except through jihad” (Art. 13). In Art. 7 it quotes the hadith according to which the Day of Judgement will not come until the Muslims fight the Jews and the Jews hide behind stones and trees, and the stones and trees say “O Muslim, there is a Jew behind me, come and kill him”. Art. 22 attributes to the Jews control of the world's press and money, the French and Communist revolutions, the two world wars, the League of Nations and the UN, and presents them as being behind Freemasonry and Rotary Clubs; Art. 32 cites the Protocols of the Elders of Zion as proof.

fuentes/carta-de-hamas/por_que_importa.texto: It is the central document for understanding Hamas's ideology and one of the most widely distributed antisemitic texts of the late 20th century. In 2017 Hamas published a document of principles that distinguishes between Jews and Zionists, but it never formally repealed the 1988 charter.

fuentes/carta-de-hamas/leer.0.titulo.texto: Full English translation (Avalon Project, Yale Law School)

fuentes/declaracion-de-independencia-pal.texto: Proclamation of the State of Palestine by the Palestinian National Council, drafted by Mahmoud Darwish and read by Arafat in Algiers; it invokes Resolution 181, which “still provides conditions of international legitimacy” for a Palestinian Arab state.

fuentes/acuerdos-de-oslo/resumen.texto: Framework agreement between Israel and the PLO: Israeli withdrawal from Gaza and Jericho, an elected Palestinian authority, a five-year transition and negotiations on final status (Jerusalem, refugees, settlements, borders), which were to conclude in 1999. It was preceded by letters of mutual recognition between Rabin and Arafat.

fuentes/tratado-de-paz-israel-jordania/r.texto: It sets the border and the sharing of the waters of the Jordan and the Yarmouk, and recognizes Jordan's special role in the Muslim holy sites of Jerusalem.

fuentes/hoja-de-ruta/autor.texto: The United States, the European Union, Russia and the UN

fuentes/hoja-de-ruta/resumen.texto: Three-phase plan by the Quartet towards two states by 2005: an end to Palestinian violence and a freeze on settlements, a provisional Palestinian state, and a final agreement. It never got beyond the first phase.

fuentes/documento-de-hamas-2017/titulo.texto: Document of General Principles and Policies of Hamas (2017)
